writing.label: Written by Bob Dylan — not Adele
trail: The song is credited to Bob Dylan, who wrote it for his 1997 album Time Out of Mind.
Adele’s 2008 recording is so identified with her — it was one of her early signatures — that many take it for her own composition. She recorded it; Dylan wrote it.
The same page’s other story is the recording (above): Dylan’s song was first released by other artists in 1997, and Adele’s is the version most listeners now know.

meta.ogTitle: Who originally recorded 'Make You Feel My Love'?
meta.ogDescription: Bob Dylan wrote it; Billy Joel released it first, in August 1997. Adele's 2008 recording is a cover, not the original.

answer.label: Not an Adele original — the first release was Billy Joel’s, in August 1997
answer.sourceLine: Adele’s 2008 recording is so completely identified with her that the song is routinely assumed to be hers from the start. It is not: the song was written by Bob Dylan, and the first version the public could buy was Billy Joel’s “To Make You Feel My Love,” issued as a single on 13 August 1997 and included on Greatest Hits Volume III (Columbia Records, 19 August 1997). Dylan’s own recording followed on Time Out of Mind, released 30 September 1997. Joel’s single was a modest chart entry — No. 50 on the Billboard Hot 100, No. 9 Adult Contemporary — and has been almost entirely eclipsed.

original.charted: No. 50 on the US Billboard Hot 100; No. 9 on the US Adult Contemporary chart. A real but minor showing — nowhere near enough to fix the song to Joel’s name.
original.cover: Adele’s recording, from her debut album 19, was released as a single on 27 October 2008 on XL Recordings (Columbia in the US). It first peaked at No. 26 in the UK, then re-entered after The X Factor performances in 2010 and reached No. 4, going multi-platinum.

authors.name: Billy Joel
authors.heading: The version that got there first
authors.bio: Joel had spent the 1990s stepping back from pop songwriting, and Greatest Hits Volume III was padded out with a small handful of covers — unusual for a catalogue built almost entirely on his own material. One of them was a brand-new Bob Dylan song. Issued as a single on 13 August 1997, it reached No. 50 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 9 on Adult Contemporary, and then quietly disappeared underneath everything that came after it.

authors.name: Adele
authors.heading: The version everyone knows
authors.bio: Adele recorded the song for her debut album 19 at her manager’s suggestion, and it was released as a single on 27 October 2008. It initially reached No. 26 in the UK; after it was performed on The X Factor in 2010 it re-entered and climbed to No. 4, going on to multi-platinum certification. Her reading — voice and piano, almost nothing else — is the definitive one for most listeners, which is exactly why the chronology gets lost. Nothing about the record is wrong; only the assumption that it came first.

authors.name: Bob Dylan
authors.heading: The man who wrote it
authors.metaLine: b. 1941 · American songwriter · wrote the song for Time Out of Mind
authors.bio: Dylan wrote the song for Time Out of Mind, the Daniel Lanois-produced album whose official sessions began at Criteria Studios in Miami in January 1997. His own recording of it therefore existed before Joel’s single appeared — but it was not heard by anyone until the album came out on 30 September 1997, after Joel’s. Dylan is the one constant across every version of this song, and the one most casual listeners never connect to it at all.

misattribution.heading: The record, straightened out
misattribution.intro: Adele’s 2008 recording is the one almost everyone means when they name this song, and it is routinely assumed to be where the song began. Here is the actual order of events.

items.why: Recorded for her debut album 19 and released as a single on 27 October 2008. It reached No. 26 in the UK, then re-entered and climbed to No. 4 in 2010 after The X Factor. A cover from the first take — and the album’s track listing says so.

Issued as a single on 13 August 1997 and included on Greatest Hits Volume III (Columbia Records, 19 August 1997) as “To Make You Feel My Love.” It reached No. 50 on the Billboard Hot 100 and No. 9 on Adult Contemporary. This is the first version the public could hear.

Dylan wrote the song and cut his own version during the Time Out of Mind sessions, which began at Criteria Studios in January 1997 — before Joel’s single appeared. But that album was not released until 30 September 1997. So the earliest recording made is almost certainly Dylan’s; the earliest recording released is Joel’s.
Both recorded it for the 1998 Hope Floats soundtrack. Brooks’ version reached No. 1 on the US country chart — a substantial hit that has itself been largely forgotten behind Adele’s.

misattribution.truthLine: Bob Dylan wrote it. Billy Joel released it first, in August 1997. Adele’s 2008 version is the famous one — and it is a cover.

context.heading: Why the cover swallowed the original
lead: The interesting thing here is not that Adele covered a song — it is that she covered a song nobody had claimed. Joel’s single was a chart footnote on a compilation album; Dylan’s version sat as track nine on a late-career record admired more than it was played. Neither had planted a flag. When Adele recorded it for 19 at her manager’s suggestion, she was not competing with a famous original — she was filling a vacancy.

There was also a large country detour in between: Garth Brooks and Trisha Yearwood both cut the song for the 1998 Hope Floats soundtrack, and Brooks’ version went to No. 1 on the US country chart. That the song could pass through a No. 1 country hit and still arrive at Adele looking like a blank slate says something about how completely a performance can overwrite a copyright.
detailsBody: January 1997 — the official Time Out of Mind sessions begin at Criteria Studios in Miami, with Daniel Lanois producing. Dylan’s own recording of the song dates from these sessions.
13 August 1997 — Billy Joel’s “To Make You Feel My Love” is issued as a single. This is the first time the public hears the song.
19 August 1997 — Greatest Hits Volume III is released on Columbia Records with the track included.
30 September 1997 — Dylan’s Time Out of Mind is released, containing his own version.
1998 — Garth Brooks and Trisha Yearwood both record it for the Hope Floats soundtrack; Brooks’ version tops the US country chart.
28 January 2008 — Adele’s debut album 19 is released on XL Recordings with the song as track nine.
27 October 2008 — Adele’s version is released as a single. It first peaks at No. 26 in the UK.
2010 — after performances on The X Factor, the single re-enters the UK chart and reaches No. 4, becoming the version the song is now known by.
context.pull: Adele did not displace an original. She filled a vacancy.

schema.faqAnswer: No. Adele's 2008 version is a cover. Bob Dylan wrote the song, and the first commercially released recording was Billy Joel's "To Make You Feel My Love", issued as a single on 13 August 1997. Dylan's own recording was made earlier, during the January 1997 Time Out of Mind sessions, but was not released until 30 September 1997.
